title: Math roguelite about counting sheep to kill the nightmares
author: Toamig
selftext:
Hey guys! This is my take on a game that started as a math puzzle game. Eventually I themed it about counting sheep to kill the nightmares so we could finally get a cozy night and rest.   
Over the time I saw the puzzle idea I had was becoming too exhausting due to the amount of math so I converted it into a roguelite where I started drawing a lot of inspiration from Balatro and Slay the Spire. 

At this point I'm working on the game feel to make everything feel juicier, including this payoff moment. 

Apart from some SFXs that need improvement, what are your thoughts so far? Do you feel like playing it, based on this short clip? Is it too exaggerated or on point?

comments.author: SillyHamm
comments.body: the visuals and SFX are amazing! very satisfying

replies.author: Toamig
replies.body:
Thank you so much! ☺️🙏 if you’d like you can try the demo on itch.io - https://toamig.itch.io/lucky-flock  
It’s free and playable on the browser. I’m looking for feedback and I’d be much appreciated

comments.author: nikitagr
comments.body: How did you make sounds and effects?

replies.author: Toamig
replies.body:
A bunch of iterations with Claude. Now I’m using GPT image generation to improve them as I find GPT better with art matters.

I try to give references for what I want to achieve and a bunch of context and let the AI experiment then I evaluate and chose a path. Claude is good at generating synth audio but here it doesn’t fit so I told it to scan and search SFXs that can be adequate for what I want and then I select. Eventually something is good enough and I can just tell it to remix or change tones, apply filters etc etc until it matches the mood I want.

replies.author: Toamig
replies.body: Thank you so much 🙏 there’s still a long road ahead until I release it. But there’s a free demo on itch if you’d like to try ☺️ it’s called lucky flock
